  Procedures for Addressing the Council

  8.  APPROVAL OF THE WARRANT REGISTER
  Comments:
  City of Lynwood warrant register dated October 20, 2020 for FY 2020-2021. (FIN)

  Staff recommends that the City Council of the City of Lynwood approve the warrant register dated
  October 20, 2020 for FY 2020-2021.

  9.  PRINTING SERVICE CONTRACT FOR THE CITY NEWSLETTER (LNP)
  Comments:
  In August 2019, the City entered into a one (1) year extension agreement with Queen Beach
  Printers for the printing of the City’s monthly community newsletter, LNP. The contracted
  payments to Queen Beach Printers are approximately $3,480 per issue for 17,000 full color
  prints. The City Council will be considering extending this agreement for an additional year without
  an increase in the price per issue. (CM)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached entitled resolution: " A RESOLUTION
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNW OOD, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE
  OF CALIFORNIA AUTHORIZING A ONE (1) YEAR CONTRACT EXTENSION FOR THE
  PRINTING SERVICES FOR THE CITY NEW SLETTER (LNP)."

  10.  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD EXTENDING
  THE EXISTENCE OF LOCAL EMERGENCY
  Comments:
  The City Council will consider the extension of Emergency regarding COVID-19 Pandemic. (HR)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council take the following actions:

   1. Adopt the attached resolution entitled “A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF LYNWOOD, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA,
  EXTENDING THE EXISTENCE OF A LOCAL EMERGENCY RELATING TO THE
  COVID-19 PANDEMIC.”;
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable; and
  3. Receive and File Status Update for Local Emergency as per Government Code §8630.

  11.  ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 1738 ADDING SECTION 3-36 “UNLAWFUL
  SPECTATING AT STREET RACES, MOTOR VEHICLE SPEED CONTESTS, AND
  SIDESHOWS” TO THE LYNWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE (“LMC”) PROHIBITING
  SPECTATORS AT MOTOR VEHICLE SPEED CONTESTS, STREET RACING
  EVENTS, AND SIDESHOWS” TO THE LYNWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE
  Comments:
  The City Council will consider the adoption of Ordinance No. 1738, which would prohibit
  spectators from being present at street racing, speed contests, or sideshows (i.e. burnouts,
  donuts, etc.). (CD)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council waive the second reading and adopt Ordinance No. 1738
  entitled “UNLAWFUL SPECTATING AT STREET RACES, MOTOR VEHICLE SPEED
  CONTESTS, AND SIDESHOWS” TO THE LYNWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE (“LMC”)
  PROHIBITING SPECTATORS AT MOTOR VEHICLE SPEED CONTESTS, STREET
  RACING EVENTS, AND SIDESHOWS.”

  12.  AUTHORIZATION TO APPLY FOR PROPOSITION 68 GRANT PROGRAM FUNDS
  Comments:
  The purpose of this item is to request authorization from the Lynwood City Council to apply for
  grant programs, under Proposition 68 (Parks and Water Bond Act of 2018), that the City of
  Lynwood is eligible for and that staff finds prudent to submit an application. Per grant
  requirements, the Proposition 68 Grant Program requires a general authorizing resolution from
  the City’s governing body to apply for and receive grant funding. (REC)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A RESOLUTION
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNW OOD, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE
  OF CALIFORNIA, APPROVING APPLICATION(S) FOR PER CAPITA GRANT FUNDS.”

  13.  RESPONSE TO THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY CIVIL GRAND JURY REPORT
  ENTITLED “A DIET FOR LANDFILLS: CUTTING DOWN ON FOOD WASTE”
  Comments:
  On July 8, 2020, the Los Angeles County Civil Grand Jury released a report entitled “A DIET
  FOR LANDFILLS: Cutting Down on Food Waste.” It is to staff’s knowledge that the Los Angeles
  Civil Grand Jury sent out letters to the mayors of cities in Los Angeles County, requiring a
  response to all the recommendations in a Civil Grand Jury report. In accordance with California
  Penal Code § 933.05-06, the City is required to provide a response to a number of suggested
  programs and actions designed to improve organics recycling. With assistance from the City
  Attorney, a proposed response to the report has been prepared. Staff recommends that the City
  Council authorizes the Mayor to sign the response and for the Acting City Manager or her
  designee to submit the response. (PW)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A RESOLUTION
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES,

  DOWN ON FOOD WASTE, AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR TO SIGN THE WRITTEN
  RESPONSE, AND AUTHORIZING THE ACTING CITY MANAGER OR HER DESIGNEE
  TO SUBMIT THE SIGNED WRITTEN RESPONSE TO THE PRESIDING JUDGE OF THE
  LOS ANGELES SUPERIOR COURT.”

  NEW/OLD BUSINESS
  14.  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD, COUNTY OF
  LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA, TO AUTHORIZE THE ELIMINATION OF
  TWENTY-FOUR (24) FILLED AND VACANT POSITIONS AND TO AUTHORIZE THE
  ACTING CITY MANAGER TO IMPLEMENT THE RESULTING LAYOFFS AND
  AUTHORIZE THE ACTING CITY MANAGER TO IMPLEMENT A MODIFIED LAYOFF
  BASED ON IMPROVED ECONOMIC CONDITIONS
  Comments:
  The COVID-19 pandemic has significantly impacted the economy at both the state and local
  levels and has significantly impacted local government revenues and increased reliance on
  government programs due to a significant unemployment rate. The City experienced a $3M
  revenue shortfall for FY19-20, necessitating expenditures be paid through the general fund
  reserves. the City is experiencing a $3.7M budget gap for FY 20-21. To close the gap, City
  Departments made more than $1M in non-personnel cuts, and implemented a hiring freeze
  expected to save an additional $1,464,495. Staff is recommending that the City Council of the
  City of Lynwood approve a resolution to implement the elimination of 24 filled and vacant
  positions and authorize the Acting City Manager to implement the layoffs. (HR)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council of the City of Lynwood take one of the following actions:

  1. Authorize a layoff by adopting the attached resolution entitled “A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF
  CALIFORNIA, TO AUTHORIZE THE ELIMINATION OF TWENTY-FOUR (24) FILLED AND
  VACANT POSITIONS AND TO AUTHORIZE THE ACTING CITY MANAGER TO
  IMPLEMENT THE RESULTING LAYOFF AND AUTHORIZE THE ACTING CITY
  MANAGER TO IMPLEMENT A MODIFED LAYOFF BASED ON IMPROVED ECONOMIC
  CONDITIONS.”

  2. Direct a more limited scope of layoff by instructing the Acting City Manager and the City’s
  negotiating team to reduce the number of positions proposed to be eliminated and to seek
  comparable reductions of salary and benefits through the bargaining process and present those
  options to City Council for further consideration.

  3. Direct the Acting City Manager and the City’s negotiating team to seek significant salary and
  benefit cuts in lieu of any proposed layoff, with the City Council retaining the option to eliminate
  positions and layoff later if agreement is not reached.

  15.  AMENDMENT TO COMMUNICATIONS CONSULTING SERVICES AGREEMENT
  Comments:
  On July 16, 2018, the City Council approved a second amendment to the contract for the Kilkenny
  Group to provide communications consulting services and manage public relations matters for the
  City of Lynwood. These services are needed to promote City programs and events, manage
  media interactions, and provide related work as requested. The consultant is requesting to amend
  the agreement extending the term until June 30, 2021. (CM)

  Recommendation:

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 4 of 146
   Staff recommends that the City Council of the City of Lynwood adopt the attached resolution
  entitled; “A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNW OOD, COUNTY
  OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA APPROVING A THIRD AMENDMENT TO THE
  KILKENNY GROUP AGREEMENT TO PROVIDE COMMUNICATIONS CONSULTING
  SERVICES TO MANAGE BROADCAST MEDIA INTERACTIONS AND OTHER PUBLIC
  RELATIONS MATTERS FOR THE CITY OF LYNW OOD FOR THE PERIOD JULY 1, 2020 -
  JUNE 30, 2021, AT A COST NOT TO EXCEED $125,000."

  16.  ESTABLISHMENT OF A MEASURE LH OVERSIGHT COMMITTEE
  Comments:
  The City Council will consider the establishment of a Measure LH Oversight Committee that
  would be responsible for reviewing expenditures of Measure LH funds, informing the public of
  these expenditures, and reporting annually to the City Council on the Committee's activity. This
  would be a proactive measure so that the City Council is prepared in the case the voters approve
  Measure LH on November 3, 2020. (CD)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the following resolution entitled: " A RESOLUTION
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNW OOD, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE
  OF CALIFORNIA AUTHORIZING A MEASURE LH OVERSIGHT COMMITTEE TO REVIEW
  EXPENDITURES OF MEASURE LH FUNDS, INFORM THE PUBLIC OF THE
  EXPENDITURES, AND REPORT ANNUALLY TO THE CITY COUNCIL ON THE OVERSIGHT
  COMMITTEE’S ACTIVITY.”

  17.  AUTHORIZATION TO ESTABLISH CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECT - SKATE
  PARK/PUMP TRACK FACILITY AT BURKE-HAM PARK
  Comments:
  The Lynwood City Council adopted Resolution #2019.117 that provides funding for park
  improvements within the City. Staff is requesting that the City Council authorize the establishment
  of a Capital Improvement Project for the Burke-Ham Park Skate Park-Pump Track Project as
  well as adopt a Project Budget. (REC)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the accompanying resolution entitled, “A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD, COUNTY OF LOS
  ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA AUTHORIZING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A
  CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECT AND PROJECT BUDGET FOR THE SKATE
  PARK-PUMP TRACK PROJECT AT BURKE-HAM PARK.”

  CITY COUNCIL ORAL AND WRITTEN COMMUNICATION
  ADJOURNMENT
  THE NEXT REGULAR MEETING WILL BE HELD ON NOVEMBER 3, 2020 AT 6:00 P.M. IN THE
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS OF THE CITY HALL ANNEX, 11350 BULLIS ROAD, CITY OF
  LYNWOOD, CALIFORNIA.

  SUBJECT:  PRINTING SERVICE CONTRACT FOR THE CITY NEWSLETTER (LNP)

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached entitled resolution: " A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNW OOD, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA
  AUTHORIZING A ONE (1) YEAR CONTRACT EXTENSION FOR THE PRINTING SERVICES FOR THE CITY
  NEW SLETTER (LNP)."

  Background:

  In August 2019, the City entered into a one (1) year extension agreement with Queen Beach Printers for the
  printing of the City’s monthly community newsletter, LNP. The agreement was approved for a not to exceed
  amount of 42,000 payments. The approximate cost is $3,480 per issue, which includes the production of 17,000
  full color prints. The agreement allows for another one (1) extension for a continuation of services without an
  increase in the price per issue.

  Discussion and Analysis:

  In order to ensure a continuation of service and to avoid any disruption in the printing of City Newsletters, staff is
  recommending that the City Council extend the existing contract for one (1) year at a not to exceed amount of
  $42,000. Queen Beach Printers is in agreement with the extension at no additional cost. The new agreement
  would expire on July 30, 2021.

   Discussion and Analysis:

  According to the State of California, organic waste comprises two-thirds of the State’s waste stream. Organic
  waste includes green waste, wood waste, food waste, fibers, such as paper and cardboard for the purposes of SB
  1383. According to CalRecycle’s last waste characterization study in 2014, food waste comprised 18 percent of
  what we disposed. Landfilling organic waste leads to the anaerobic breakdown of that material, which creates
  methane. Landfills are responsible for 21 percent of the state’s methane emissions. Landfills are the third largest
  producer of methane.

  State’s Existing Organics Recycling Mandates

  Over the years, the State has imposed strict recycling and diversion mandates to reduce organic waste that are
  disposed to the landfill.

  Under AB 1826, Mandatory Organics Recycling (MORe), the State has mandated businesses and multi-family
  entities to recycle organic waste on and after April 1, 2016, depending on the amount of waste they generate per
  week. Currently, all businesses and multi-family entities generating 2 cubic yards of waste a week, are now
  required to comply with AB1826.

  Under AB 827, the State requires commercial waste and organic waste generators to provide recycling and
  organic waste bins to customers. This law targets businesses that sell products meant for immediate
  consumption.

  Under SB 1383, jurisdictions are required to provide organic waste collection to all residents and businesses,
  establish an edible food recovery program that recovers edible food from the waste stream, conduct outreach and
  education to all affected parties, including generators, haulers, facilities, edible food recovery organizations and
  city departments, procure recycled organic waste products like compost, mulch, and renewable natural gas, and
  inspect and enforce compliance with SB 1383. SB 1383 regulations will become enforceable in January 2022.

  Response to the Grand Jury Report

  The City’s response to the Report references many efforts the City has already undertaken to recycle organics
  under AB 1826. (Exhibit A) The proposed response also addressed the recommendations included in the Grand
  Jury Report for the cities’ response such as weekly food waste drop-off center, creating an incentive program for
  residents and businesses to separate food waste, and adoption of the March 2018 Countywide Organics Waste
  Management Plan.

  Staff's proposed responses to the recommendations under the Grand Jury Report are to further analyze the
  recommendations within a six month timeframe from the release of the Grand Jury Report, to implement the
  recommendation that the City plans to implement to comply with the requirements under SB 1383, or currently
  implementing recommendations if requirements are already required under AB1826.

  Background:

  The City Council of the City of Lynwood adopted a two-year biennial budget on July 2, 2019, for FY 19-20 and FY
  20-21. The Budget is the City’s operating plan that establishes the City’s goals, budget priorities, and desired

  budget was based on certain assumptions and meeting expenditure and revenue projections at the time of the
  budget adoption.

  The COVID-19 pandemic has significantly impacted the economy at both the state and local levels and has
  significantly impacted local government revenues and increased reliance on government programs due to a
  significant unemployment rate.

  During the development of the Fiscal Year (FY) 2020-21 budget, staff estimated the FY2019-20 revenue would be
  $5.2 million less than prior projections, and the FY 2020-21 revenue would decrease by another $1.6 million. As of
  September 30, 2020, the unaudited FY 2019-20 revenues only decreased by approximately $3M (as opposed to
  the original $5.2M estimate). Staff continues to forecast decreases of $1.6M for FY2020-21. The combined result
  is a permanent loss of $4.6M, which is equivalent to thirteen percent (13%) of the City’s annual General Fund
  budget. Although these projections are based on the best financial data available to the City, the actual impact of
  COVID-19 on the City’s revenue is not certain.

  The table below shows the adopted revenue, expenditures and transfers in and out for the General Fund for FY 19-
  20, adopted FY 20-21 and the revised figures based on the COVID-19 pandemic.

  In order to meet the projected shortfall, the City took the following measures:

  1. Froze all vacant positions for an annual savings of $1,464,495;
  2. Made non-personnel cuts of $1,060,276;
  3. Proposed additional cuts of filled positions for a total of $1,107,002 (i.e., layoff); and,
  4. Implemented a 5% wage reduction for non-represented employees.

  Discussion and Analysis:

  As directed by City Council, the City’s negotiating team, comprised of the Human Resources Director and the
  City’s labor relations counsel, met and conferred with both bargaining units to see if they would be willing to offer

  layoffs. Staff met with the both the Lynwood Employees’ Association and the Lynwood Employees’ Management
  Group approximately ten times during the months of July, August, September and October. Both groups made
  proposals to offset the proposed layoffs. However, the proposals made by both groups have been short of the
  needed cost-savings and rejected by the Lynwood City Council in closed session on October 6, 2020.

  The City experienced a $3M revenue shortfall for FY19-20, necessitating expenditures be paid through the
  general fund reserves. As shown on prior table, the City’s general fund unaudited reserves have decreased from
  over $7M to under $6M. As stated prior, the City is experiencing a $3.7M budget gap for FY 20-21. To close the

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the following resolution entitled: " A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNW OOD, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA
  AUTHORIZING A MEASURE LH OVERSIGHT COMMITTEE TO REVIEW EXPENDITURES OF MEASURE LH
  FUNDS, INFORM THE PUBLIC OF THE EXPENDITURES, AND REPORT ANNUALLY TO THE CITY COUNCIL
  ON THE OVERSIGHT COMMITTEE’S ACTIVITY.”

  Background:

  On August 4, 2020, the City Council initiate the process to levy an annual excise tax on each hospital engaging in
  business within City limits, known as Measure LH. The tax to be imposed will be an amount equivalent to three
  percent (3%) of the hospital’s gross receipts. In anticipation of the passage of Measure LH, it is being proposed
  that the City Council establish a Measure LH Oversight Committee that would be responsible for reviewing
  expenditures of Measure LH funds, informing the public of these expenditures, and reporting annually to the City
  Council on the Committee's activity.

  Discussion and Analysis:

  Currently, the City Council appoints citizens to serve on a variety of Boards, Commissions, and Committees that
  have been established under Chapter 2 “Administration” of the Lynwood Municipal Code (LMC). Standing
  members serve at the pleasure of the City Council and each Council Member appoints one (1) person to serve to
  represent that county Member’s interest with the community.

  The City Council recently took action to place Measure LH on the November 3rd ballot as a tax on for-profit
  hospitals. Measure LH is a general tax. A general tax refers to a general levy by a government that offers no
  special benefit to the taxpayer, but instead support to governmental programs that benefit all. Proceeds from the
  Measure LH would be deposited into the City’s general fund and could be used for any and all municipal
  purposes. Measure LH would be operative if a majority of the electors voting on the measure vote to approve the

  In anticipation of the passage of Measure LH, it is being recommended that the City Council authorize the
  establishment of a Measure LH Oversight Committee that would be responsible for reviewing expenditures of
  Measure LH funds, informing the public of these expenditures, and reporting annually to the City Council on the
  Committee's activity.

  Fiscal Impact:

  To be consistent with the other established Boards, Commissions, and Committees, compensation for the
  Measure LH Committee will be set at $50 per meeting attended, as outlined in the attached Resolution. In
  addition, funds would need to be allocated for operation of the Measure LH Oversight Committee, which would not
  exceed $1,250. The source of funding would be from the unappropriated general fund balance.

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the accompanying resolution entitled, “A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA
  AUTHORIZING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECT AND PROJECT

  Background:

  The Lynwood City Council adopted Resolution #2019.117 that provides funding for park improvements within the
  City. Staff is requesting that the City Council authorize the establishment of a Capital Improvement Project for the
  Burke-Ham Park Skate Park-Pump Track Project as well as adopt a Project Budget.

  Discussion and Analysis:

  From the hundreds of Lynwood skaters that attended the City’s 20th Anniversary of the Lynwood Skate Park event
  in February 2020, to the seven million plus skaters across the country, skating remains very popular. Interest in the
  sport is expected to increase even more in 2021 when skateboarding will make its debut at the Summer Olympic
  Games in Tokyo.

  There is a popular saying among municipal administrators that says, “If your town doesn’t have a skate park, it is
  one.” Opened in February of 2020, the existing skate park at Lynwood City Park was one of the first in the
  Southeast Los Angeles area. However, the community demand for skate facilities quickly outgrew the City’s
  relatively small and only skate park.

  Studies show that the majority of skateboarding injuries occur because of surface irregularities and collisions with
  vehicles or pedestrians. If no skate park is available, skateboarders tend to use whatever structures are available
  to them, even with “no skateboarding allowed” signs posted. Having a designated space for skating activities not
